sentences.en: This is 99% Invisible.
sentences.zh: 这里是《99%隐形》。

sentences.en: I'm Roman Mars.
sentences.zh: 我是罗曼·马斯。

sentences.en: It's the most wonderful time of the year.
sentences.zh: 这是一年中最美妙的时光。

sentences.en: It's mini-story season.
sentences.zh: 这是迷你故事季。

sentences.en: Gather the kids around the fire because we have a year-end mix of short stories about a rogue architect,
sentences.zh: 把孩子们聚在火炉旁吧，因为我们准备了一份年终短篇故事合集，关于一位特立独行的建筑师、

sentences.en: spooky kitchens, a hundred-year-old music streaming service,
sentences.zh: 阴森的厨房、一个百年历史的音乐流媒体服务，

sentences.en: and the crazy way the French try to make telling time less crazy.
sentences.zh: 以及法国人试图让计时方式变得不那么疯狂的疯狂尝试。

sentences.en: Let's go.
sentences.zh: 我们开始吧。

sentences.en: So we are here with producer Chris Berube.
sentences.zh: 现在我们和制作人克里斯·伯鲁比在一起。

sentences.en: Hey, Chris.
sentences.zh: 嘿，克里斯。

sentences.en: Hello, Roman.
sentences.zh: 你好，罗曼。

sentences.en: What do you have for us?
sentences.zh: 你给我们带来了什么？

sentences.en: Okay, so I've been very into the French Revolution recently.
sentences.zh: 好的，我最近对法国大革命非常着迷。

sentences.en: I know there's been these online trends of people reading up about the Roman Empire,
sentences.zh: 我知道网上一直有关于人们阅读古罗马帝国历史的趋势，

sentences.en: but, you know, I'm a little different.
sentences.zh: 但是，你知道，我有点不一样。

sentences.en: I'm kind of zigging where other people are zagging.
sentences.zh: 当别人走寻常路时，我喜欢另辟蹊径。

sentences.en: I don't know if you knew this about me.
sentences.zh: 我不知道你是否了解我这一点。

sentences.en: I didn't know this.
sentences.zh: 我确实不知道。

sentences.en: I mean, why exactly are you reading about the French Revolution?
sentences.zh: 我是说，你到底为什么要读法国大革命？

sentences.en: I don't know.
sentences.zh: 我不知道。

sentences.en: I mean, I've been on a bit of a history kick.
sentences.zh: 我是说，我最近有点历史狂热。

sentences.en: And the French Revolution is interesting.
sentences.zh: 而且法国大革命很有趣。

sentences.en: I mean, the French revolutionaries, they saw themselves as the beginning of history, right?
sentences.zh: 我是说，法国革命者，他们把自己视为历史的开端，对吧？

sentences.en: Like, this is a whole new way of doing things.
sentences.zh: 就像是，这是一种全新的做事方式。

sentences.en: They're just trying lots of new things, like new system of government, a reign of terror, just new everything.
sentences.zh: 他们只是在尝试很多新事物，比如新的政府体制、恐怖统治，简直一切都是新的。

sentences.en: A new country with new laws and new ways of working that was very rational.
sentences.zh: 一个拥有新法律和新工作方式的新国家，非常理性。

sentences.en: Roman, that is Don Norman, the author of a book called The Design of Everyday Things and a favorite of 99% Invisible.
sentences.zh: 罗曼，那是唐·诺曼，《设计心理学》一书的作者，也是《99%隐形》最喜欢的嘉宾之一。

sentences.en: Absolutely.
sentences.zh: 绝对是。

sentences.en: I mean, my friend in college giving me a copy of The Design of Everyday Things is probably one of the reasons why this show exists.
sentences.zh: 我是说，大学时朋友送我一本《设计心理学》，这可能就是这个节目存在的原因之一。

sentences.en: I mean, he's that pivotal.
sentences.zh: 我是说，他就是这么关键。

sentences.en: He's like our spiritual godfather.
sentences.zh: 他就像我们的精神教父。

sentences.en: Totally.
sentences.zh: 完全同意。

sentences.en: And Don actually talks about the French Revolution in that book, because as part of this new rational society they were building,
sentences.zh: 唐在那本书里确实谈到了法国大革命，因为作为他们正在构建的这个新理性社会的一部分，

sentences.en: the French introduced an idea called decimalization, which is a system of measurements that uses 10 as the base number.
sentences.zh: 法国人引入了一个叫“十进制化”的概念，这是一种以10为基数的度量衡系统。

sentences.en: So they switched everything.
sentences.zh: 所以他们把一切都改了。

sentences.en: That's where kilograms, that's where grams and kilograms comes from, and meters.
sentences.zh: 这就是千克、克和米的由来。

sentences.en: So the idea behind that is when things are divisible by 10, it's just easier to do math.
sentences.zh: 所以背后的想法是，当事物能被10整除时，做数学运算就更容易了。

sentences.en: Guess what?
sentences.zh: 你猜怎么着？

sentences.en: I have 10 fingers.
sentences.zh: 我有10根手指。

sentences.en: So this base system of 10, decimalization, is where the metric system comes in.
sentences.zh: 所以这个以10为基数的系统，即十进制化，就是公制系统的来源。

sentences.en: They also had this idea for something called decimal time.
sentences.zh: 他们还有一个关于“十进制时间”的想法。

sentences.en: Huh.
sentences.zh: 嗯。

sentences.en: Correct.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: I am familiar with that one.
sentences.zh: 我对那个很熟悉。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: So we've had that for a really long time.
sentences.zh: 所以我们已经有这个想法很久了。

sentences.en: However, after the French Revolution, the legislative body, the convention, they wanted to try this new system of time that was based on decimalization.
sentences.zh: 然而，法国大革命后，立法机构——国民公会，他们想尝试这种基于十进制的新时间系统。

sentences.en: They're like, this is a new idea.
sentences.zh: 他们觉得，这是一个新点子。

sentences.en: Ignoring the fact China had something similar to this up until the 17th century, but ignore that, ignore that.
sentences.zh: 忽略了中国在17世纪之前就有类似的东西，但忽略那个，忽略那个。

sentences.en: This is the French, you know, they're saying this is our new idea.
sentences.zh: 这是法国人，你知道，他们说这是我们的新点子。

sentences.en: And this whole system, everything had a base of 10.
sentences.zh: 而整个系统，一切都以10为基数。

sentences.en: So basically everything could be divided by 10.
sentences.zh: 所以基本上一切都可以被10整除。

sentences.en: They tried to say, well, let's see, there should be 10 days in the week, right?
sentences.zh: 他们试着说，好吧，让我们看看，一周应该有10天，对吧？

sentences.en: And there should be 10 hours in the day.
sentences.zh: 一天应该有10个小时。

sentences.en: Okay.
sentences.zh: 好的。

sentences.en: Wow.
sentences.zh: 哇。

sentences.en: There's a lot to sort of like figure out all the repercussions of that.
sentences.zh: 要弄清楚所有这些带来的连锁反应还有很多工作要做。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是啊。

sentences.en: Okay.
sentences.zh: 好的。

sentences.en: So 10 day weeks.
sentences.zh: 所以是一周10天。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: So 10 days a week.
sentences.zh: 所以一周10天。

sentences.en: And actually it wasn't called a week in the system.
sentences.zh: 实际上在这个系统中它不叫周。

sentences.en: It was called a decade just to make everything a little more confusing.
sentences.zh: 它被称为“旬”，只是为了让一切变得更令人困惑。

sentences.en: Okay.
sentences.zh: 好的。

sentences.en: And the biggest challenge, it's this idea of the 10 hour day.
sentences.zh: 而最大的挑战，就是这个10小时一天的概念。

sentences.en: So 10 hour days, each hour would have 100 minutes.
sentences.zh: 所以10小时一天，每小时有100分钟。

sentences.en: Each minute would have 100 seconds.
sentences.zh: 每分钟有100秒。

sentences.en: Okay.
sentences.zh: 好的。

sentences.en: And you might've noticed that doesn't quite add up to the same length of a day that we have right now.
sentences.zh: 你可能已经注意到，这和我们现在一天的长度不太一样。

sentences.en: 10 hour days, 100 minutes.
sentences.zh: 10小时一天，100分钟。

sentences.en: Okay.
sentences.zh: 好的。

sentences.en: That's...
sentences.zh: 那是……

sentences.en: I can see you doing the math.
sentences.zh: 我看得出你在算数。

sentences.en: I can see you struggling with the math.
sentences.zh: 我看得出你在为数学运算挣扎。

sentences.en: Is that going to be long?
sentences.zh: 那会很长吗？

sentences.en: Is that close to what we have now or longer?
sentences.zh: 那和我们现在的时间接近还是更长？

sentences.en: Longer.
sentences.zh: 更长。

sentences.en: It'd be longer.
sentences.zh: 会更长。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是啊。

sentences.en: The day would be longer in that situation.
sentences.zh: 在这种情况下，一天会更长。

sentences.en: But the way to make it work so the length of the day doesn't change is actually you could change the length of a second.
sentences.zh: 但要让它行得通，使一天的长度不变，实际上你可以改变秒的长度。

sentences.en: So instead of a second being one steamboat, it could be one steamboat.
sentences.zh: 所以与其让一秒钟等于“一秒”，不如让它变成“一秒”。

sentences.en: So like you have a shorter second and that would make the math work so the day would be the same length.
sentences.zh: 所以你有一个更短的秒，这样数学就能算通，一天的长度也就一样了。

sentences.en: Wow.
sentences.zh: 哇。

sentences.en: Okay.
sentences.zh: 好的。

sentences.en: Okay.
sentences.zh: 好的。

sentences.en: Okay.
sentences.zh: 好的。

sentences.en: So the French developed this new, more rational way of keeping time.
sentences.zh: 所以法国人开发了这种新的、更理性的计时方式。

sentences.en: But how did they get people to accept one steamboat as the length of a second?
sentences.zh: 但他们是如何让人们接受“一秒”作为秒的长度的呢？

sentences.en: Like how did you implement this?
sentences.zh: 就像你是怎么实施这个的？

sentences.en: Well, the French introduced this new calendar with like 10 day weeks and this new timekeeping system in 10 hour days in 1793.
sentences.zh: 嗯，法国人在1793年引入了这个带有10天一周和10小时一天计时系统的新日历。

sentences.en: And it didn't go great right away, to be honeSt.
sentences.zh: 老实说，一开始进展并不顺利。

sentences.en: I should say they kind of half introduced it, like officially France switched over to this new system.
sentences.zh: 我应该说他们算是半推半就地引入了它，法国官方确实切换到了这个新系统。

sentences.en: But according to accounts from the time, only some people were half using it, like people were just getting adjusted to it.
sentences.zh: 但根据当时的记录，只有一些人在勉强使用，就像人们才刚刚开始适应它。

sentences.en: And to help ease the transition, they actually made up these special clocks that had both the systems of time on the clock face.
sentences.zh: 为了缓解过渡，他们实际上制作了这些特殊的时钟，表盘上同时有两种时间系统。

sentences.en: So Roman, take a look at this.
sentences.zh: 所以罗曼，看看这个。

sentences.en: Okay.
sentences.zh: 好的。

sentences.en: So the interface has 100 seconds to a minute, and then it also has the 60 seconds in an hour on the outside ring.
sentences.zh: 所以这个界面一分钟有100秒，外圈还有一小时60秒。

sentences.en: So, you know, it helps you with the conversion.
sentences.zh: 所以，你知道，它能帮你进行换算。

sentences.en: That's really nice.
sentences.zh: 那真的很棒。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是啊。

sentences.en: So it's like the inside, you have like Roman numerals 1 through 10 and 1 through 100.
sentences.zh: 所以就像在内圈，你有1到10和1到100的罗马数字。

sentences.en: And then on the outside, you have, you know, up to 24.
sentences.zh: 然后在外面，你有，你知道，最多24。

sentences.en: So you have the 24 hour clock on the outside and the 10 hour clock on the inside.
sentences.zh: 所以外圈是24小时时钟，内圈是10小时时钟。

sentences.en: And the idea was you can look at it and see both at the same time.
sentences.zh: 想法就是你可以看着它，同时看到两种时间。

sentences.en: So it's kind of this nicely designed object.
sentences.zh: 所以这算是一个设计精良的物体。

sentences.en: It's very elegant, I think.
sentences.zh: 我觉得它非常优雅。

sentences.en: It's clever.
sentences.zh: 很巧妙。

sentences.en: It's complex, but the complexity is for a reason.
sentences.zh: 它很复杂，但这种复杂是有原因的。

sentences.en: So it's a transitional piece.
sentences.zh: 所以这是一个过渡性的物件。

sentences.en: So, you know, given that you had these nice little clocks sent out to people to help them convert, what was the resistance like?
sentences.zh: 那么，既然你给人们发了这些漂亮的小时钟来帮助他们转换，那抵触情绪如何？

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是啊。

sentences.en: I mean, just imagine completely switching your understanding of time in a day.
sentences.zh: 我是说，试想一下完全改变你对一天时间的理解。

sentences.en: I mean, the issues are kind of exactly what you'd expect.
sentences.zh: 我是说，问题和你预想的差不多。

sentences.en: Like there's international trade.
sentences.zh: 比如有国际贸易。

sentences.en: So you can't really sync up with other countries that are using a completely different way of timekeeping, right?
sentences.zh: 所以你无法真正与使用完全不同计时方式的其他国家同步，对吧？

sentences.en: Second, it's annoying.
sentences.zh: 其次，这很烦人。

sentences.en: You know, it's expensive to replace all the clocks, even if you have these nice elegant, you know, two-faced clocks.
sentences.zh: 你知道，更换所有的时钟很昂贵，即使你有这些漂亮优雅的双面时钟。

sentences.en: And I mean, the biggest thing is like people are stubborn about it, right?
sentences.zh: 而且我是说，最主要的是人们对此很固执，对吧？

sentences.en: Like in this system, a decimal hour would be the equivalent of two hours and 24 minutes.
sentences.zh: 在这个系统中，一个十进制小时相当于两小时24分钟。

sentences.en: Yeah, that does not feel natural.
sentences.zh: 是啊，那感觉不自然。

sentences.en: I mean, it's like the length of a new Hollywood movie these days.
sentences.zh: 我是说，这就像现在一部新好莱坞电影的长度。

sentences.en: Like the shortest Marvel movie would be an hour.
sentences.zh: 比如最短的漫威电影会是一个小时。

sentences.en: It would be one hour long.
sentences.zh: 它会是一个小时长。

sentences.en: Well, the way I like to think about it is it's somewhere between Barbie and Oppenheimer.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我喜欢把它想成介于《芭比》和《奥本海默》之间。

sentences.en: Like it's almost the difference between the two filMs.
sentences.zh: 就像是两部电影之间几乎差了这么多。

sentences.en: But that's a huge shift, right?
sentences.zh: 但这可是巨大的转变，对吧？

sentences.en: Like it's going to be this expensive, time-consuming thing, just a really big pain in the ass.
sentences.zh: 这会是一件昂贵、耗时的事情，简直是个大麻烦。

sentences.en: And also there were like no obvious benefits to changing it.
sentences.zh: 而且改变它也没有什么明显的好处。

sentences.en: Like the 12-hour, 24-hour system worked just fine.
sentences.zh: 12小时、24小时制运行得很好。

sentences.en: So people were not eager to try a new thing just for the sake of it.
sentences.zh: 所以人们并不急于为了改变而改变。

sentences.en: So when did the French abandon it?
sentences.zh: 那么法国人是什么时候放弃它的？

sentences.en: So they had the calendar, right?
sentences.zh: 他们有日历，对吧？

sentences.en: They had the calendar with 10-day weeks and all that.
sentences.zh: 他们有10天一周的日历等等。

sentences.en: That actually lasted into the 19th century.
sentences.zh: 那实际上持续到了19世纪。

sentences.en: That lasted for a few years.
sentences.zh: 那持续了几年。

sentences.en: But the 10-hour day, that did not really take off.
sentences.zh: 但10小时一天，并没有真正流行起来。

sentences.en: And that was actually abandoned after less than two years.
sentences.zh: 而且它实际上在不到两年后就被放弃了。

sentences.en: And so did that kill the whole idea of decimal time?
sentences.zh: 那么这是否扼杀了整个十进制时间的想法？

sentences.en: It seems like we always have these sort of moments where people reassess and try to have a more rational like counting system and measurement system and even time system.
sentences.zh: 似乎我们总是有这种时刻，人们重新评估并试图拥有更理性的计数系统、测量系统甚至时间系统。

sentences.en: So there have been proposals over the years to reintroduce decimal time.
sentences.zh: 所以多年来一直有重新引入十进制时间的提议。

sentences.en: You know, at a conference, a mathematician will be like, oh, this is an interesting idea.
sentences.zh: 你知道，在会议上，数学家会说，哦，这是一个有趣的想法。

sentences.en: Let's think about it.
sentences.zh: 让我们考虑一下。

sentences.en: But the most high-profile version of this was by the Swiss company Swatch in 1998.
sentences.zh: 但其中最引人注目的版本是瑞士斯沃琪公司在1998年提出的。

sentences.en: So as a publicity stunt, they introduced an idea they called Internet Time that would divide up the day into 1,000 Swatch Beats.
sentences.zh: 作为一种宣传噱头，他们引入了一个称为“互联网时间”的概念，将一天分为1000个“斯沃琪拍子”。

sentences.en: So, you know, decimalization divided by 10.
sentences.zh: 所以，你知道，十进制化除以10。

sentences.en: And this was actually to promote a digital watch that they were rolling out.
sentences.zh: 这实际上是为了推广他们正在推出的数字手表。

sentences.en: And like it wasn't a serious proposal, but it's actually still up on their website if you look for it.
sentences.zh: 虽然这不是一个严肃的提议，但如果你去查的话，它实际上还在他们的网站上。

sentences.en: Oh, wow.
sentences.zh: 噢，哇。

sentences.en: Ultimately, like I have been thinking a lot about this.
sentences.zh: 归根结底，我一直在深入思考这个问题。

sentences.en: And maybe there is a good argument for using base 10 for our timekeeping.
sentences.zh: 也许用十进制来计时确实是个不错的论点。

sentences.en: 10 hours, 100 minutes.
sentences.zh: 10小时制，100分钟制。

sentences.en: It's very clean.
sentences.zh: 非常简洁。

sentences.en: It's very rational.
sentences.zh: 非常理性。

sentences.en: But I don't think this proposal takes into account like how stubborn people are and also the fact that like humans just don't work that way.
sentences.zh: 但我觉得这个提议没考虑到人们有多固执，也没考虑到人类根本不是那样运作的。

sentences.en: We are not clean and rational beings.
sentences.zh: 我们并非纯粹理性的生物。

sentences.en: We're going to force our world of mechanics and digitalization and logical thinking upon poor little humans who are illogical.
sentences.zh: 我们打算把机械化、数字化和逻辑思维的世界强加给那些不讲逻辑的可怜人类。

sentences.en: They don't think logically.
sentences.zh: 他们思考问题不讲逻辑。

sentences.en: They have emotions and all that.
sentences.zh: 他们有情感，诸如此类。

sentences.en: And no wonder it didn't catch on.
sentences.zh: 难怪它没能流行起来。

sentences.en: Because logic is wonderful for the intellectuals who live in their little towers.
sentences.zh: 因为逻辑对于住在象牙塔里的知识分子来说固然美妙。

sentences.en: But not for the everyday person who wants to.
sentences.zh: 但对于想要过日子的普通人来说却并非如此。

sentences.en: Come on.
sentences.zh: 得了吧。

sentences.en: When I go to France, do they behave logically?
sentences.zh: 我去法国的时候，他们的行为符合逻辑吗？

sentences.en: No.
sentences.zh: 不。

sentences.en: We have these wonderful breakfasts.
sentences.zh: 我们享受着这些美妙的早餐。

sentences.en: They know what's important and what's not important.
sentences.zh: 他们知道什么重要，什么不重要。

sentences.en: They enjoy life.
sentences.zh: 他们懂得享受生活。

sentences.en: Yes, that sounds very true and very sort of our experience with design is like you can have big lofty ideas.
sentences.zh: 没错，这听起来很真实，而且我们在设计方面的经验也确实是这样：你可以有宏大高远的想法。

sentences.en: But in the end, when it's sort of grafted on our, you know, silly and capricious world, it just does not work.
sentences.zh: 但最终，当它被强加在我们那愚蠢又任性的世界上时，它就是行不通。

sentences.en: Yeah, exactly right.
sentences.zh: 是啊，完全正确。

sentences.en: Thank you for always bringing us, you know, silly and kind of profound ideas all in one package.
sentences.zh: 谢谢你总是带给我们这些既愚蠢又深刻的创意。

sentences.en: Oh, of course.
sentences.zh: 噢，当然。

sentences.en: Thanks, Roman.
sentences.zh: 谢谢你，Roman。

sentences.zh: 非常感谢你，库尔特（Kurt）。

sentences.en: Thank you, Roman.
sentences.zh: 谢谢你，罗曼（Roman）。

sentences.en: So, I'm here with Delaney Hall.
sentences.zh: 那么，我和德莱尼·霍尔（Delaney Hall）在一起。

sentences.en: Hey, Delaney, what's your mini story?
sentences.zh: 嘿，德莱尼，你的迷你故事是什么？

sentences.en: Hey, Roman.
sentences.zh: 嘿，罗曼。

sentences.en: So, recently, Kurt was telling me about a phenomenon called ghost kitchens.
sentences.zh: 最近，库尔特跟我讲了一个叫“幽灵厨房”的现象。

sentences.en: I had never heard of this before.
sentences.zh: 我以前从未听说过这个。

sentences.en: And it kind of exploded my whole idea about what a restaurant even is in this time.
sentences.zh: 它彻底颠覆了我对当下餐厅定义的认知。

sentences.en: And it was a very confusing experience researching these things.
sentences.zh: 研究这些东西的过程非常令人困惑。

sentences.en: And so, that's what I'd like to talk with you about today.
sentences.zh: 所以，这就是我今天想和你聊的话题。

sentences.en: Okay.
sentences.zh: 好的。

sentences.en: Okay.
sentences.zh: 好的。

sentences.en: Well, let's start with what you found.
sentences.zh: 那么，让我们从你的发现开始吧。

sentences.en: Like, what is a ghost kitchen?
sentences.zh: 什么是幽灵厨房？

sentences.en: So, ghost kitchens have a few names.
sentences.zh: 幽灵厨房有几个名字。

sentences.en: They're sometimes known as dark kitchens or virtual kitchens, cloud kitchens.
sentences.zh: 它们有时被称为暗黑厨房、虚拟厨房或云厨房。

sentences.en: And they're a relatively new trend in the restaurant industry that seemed to really take off during the pandemic.
sentences.zh: 它们是餐饮业中一种相对较新的趋势，似乎在疫情期间真正兴起。

sentences.en: That was because of the popularity of delivery services like DoorDash and Uber Eats.
sentences.zh: 这是因为DoorDash和Uber Eats等外卖服务的普及。

sentences.en: And the basic idea is that they are kitchens that specialize in delivery only.
sentences.zh: 其基本理念是，这些厨房专门从事外卖业务。

sentences.en: They do not have a storefront.
sentences.zh: 它们没有实体店面。

sentences.en: They do not have servers.
sentences.zh: 它们没有服务员。

sentences.en: They do not have a place you can walk in and sit down.
sentences.zh: 它们没有你可以走进去坐下的地方。

sentences.en: They only sell food through delivery apps.
sentences.zh: 它们只通过外卖应用程序销售食物。

sentences.en: And I can totally see why this cropped up during the pandemic.
sentences.zh: 我完全明白为什么这会在疫情期间出现。

sentences.en: Because the first, like, hardest thing to do in this world is to run a restaurant with a storefront.
sentences.zh: 因为在这个世界上，经营一家有实体店面的餐厅是最难的事情之一。

sentences.en: And then all of a sudden, your crowds are gone because you can't pack them in there because of COVID.
sentences.zh: 突然间，因为新冠疫情，你无法容纳顾客，客流就消失了。

sentences.en: But still, people need to eat.
sentences.zh: 但人们仍然需要吃饭。

sentences.en: And so, they are only doing delivery.
sentences.zh: 所以，它们只做外卖。

sentences.en: And if you're being delivered food, who cares if it's from a restaurant with a storefront or not?
sentences.zh: 如果你点的是外卖，谁会在乎它是不是来自有实体店面的餐厅呢？

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: There is totally an economic logic to it.
sentences.zh: 这完全符合经济逻辑。

sentences.en: But how do they work?
sentences.zh: 但它们是如何运作的呢？

sentences.en: Like, how do you set one up?
sentences.zh: 比如，你怎么开一家这样的店？

sentences.en: So, there are a few different types of ghost kitchens.
sentences.zh: 幽灵厨房有几种不同的类型。

sentences.en: One type is a kitchen that makes food for a bunch of different, you know, quote-unquote restaurants that all have different identities and names.
sentences.zh: 其中一种是为许多不同的、所谓的“餐厅”制作食物，这些餐厅都有不同的身份和名称。

sentences.en: And those restaurants are basically hanging their digital shingle out on services like DoorDash or Uber Eats.
sentences.zh: 这些餐厅基本上是在DoorDash或Uber Eats等服务平台上挂出数字招牌。

sentences.en: And they might appear to be different restaurants.
sentences.zh: 它们看起来可能是不同的餐厅。

sentences.en: But the reality is that all of their food is cooked in the same ghost kitchen.
sentences.zh: 但事实是，它们所有的食物都是在同一个幽灵厨房里烹制的。

sentences.en: And it's pretty interesting.
sentences.zh: 这很有趣。

sentences.en: There can be a lot of delivery-only restaurants that are all actually part of the same ghost kitchen operation.
sentences.zh: 有很多只做外卖的餐厅，实际上都是同一个幽灵厨房运营的一部分。

sentences.en: So, as an example, I watched this video by Eddie Burback.
sentences.zh: 举个例子，我看了埃迪·伯巴克（Eddie Burback）制作的视频。

sentences.en: He's a comedian and a YouTuber who did, I have to say, this surprisingly deep dive investigation into ghost kitchens.
sentences.zh: 他是一位喜剧演员和YouTuber，我必须说，他对幽灵厨房进行了令人惊讶的深入调查。

sentences.en: And he basically scanned delivery apps looking for restaurants in L.A.
sentences.zh: 他基本上是在外卖应用程序上搜索洛杉矶的餐厅，

sentences.en: that all listed the same address.
sentences.zh: 发现它们都列出了同一个地址。

sentences.en: And he found that there were a whopping 44 different restaurants that all shared the same location, which is a real tip-off that you're dealing with the ghost kitchen.
sentences.zh: 他发现竟然有44家不同的餐厅共享同一个地址，这正是你正在接触幽灵厨房的明显迹象。

sentences.en: And there was this other curious thing that Eddie Burback discovered, which is that these delivery apps, they often give the feeling of a lot of variety.
sentences.zh: 埃迪·伯巴克还发现了另一件奇怪的事情，那就是这些外卖应用程序往往给人一种种类繁多的感觉。

sentences.en: Like, there's lots of different logos and restaurant names.
sentences.zh: 比如，有很多不同的标志和餐厅名称。

sentences.en: But the funny thing is that sometimes those places all seem to be making the same food.
sentences.zh: 但有趣的是，有时这些地方似乎都在制作同样的食物。

sentences.en: And the way he discovered this is that Eddie started looking at the menu items from supposedly different restaurants that were all based at the same location.
sentences.zh: 他发现这一点的方法是，埃迪开始查看那些位于同一地址、看似不同的餐厅的菜单项。

sentences.en: And he found that they all seem to have the exact same beer-battered cod sandwich.
sentences.zh: 他发现它们似乎都有完全相同的啤酒炸鳕鱼三明治。

sentences.en: Like, it's all the same picture.
sentences.zh: 图片都是一样的。

sentences.en: It's all the same price, the exact same description, which is a beer-battered North Atlantic cod, slaw, red and white cabbage, lemon herb aioli, and a brioche bun.
sentences.zh: 价格一样，描述也完全相同，即啤酒炸北大西洋鳕鱼、凉拌卷心菜（红白卷心菜）、柠檬香草蒜泥蛋黄酱和布里欧修面包。

sentences.en: And a brioche bun.
sentences.zh: 还有布里欧修面包。

sentences.en: So I looked at another obvious choice at the same address, at Sunset Beach Fish and Chips.
sentences.zh: 所以我看了同一个地址下的另一个显眼的选择，日落海滩炸鱼薯条（Sunset Beach Fish and Chips）。

sentences.en: And would you look at that?
sentences.zh: 你瞧，那是什么？

sentences.en: There's a beer-battered cod sandwich for $16.95.
sentences.zh: 有一个售价16.95美元的啤酒炸鳕鱼三明治。

sentences.en: That is a beer-battered North Atlantic cod, slaw, red and white cabbage, lemon herb aioli, and a brioche bun.
sentences.zh: 那也是啤酒炸北大西洋鳕鱼、凉拌卷心菜（红白卷心菜）、柠檬香草蒜泥蛋黄酱和布里欧修面包。

sentences.en: Interesting.
sentences.zh: 有趣。

sentences.en: Two separate restaurants on Uber Eats, appearing to be completely separate businesses, selling the same item with the same description for the same price.
sentences.zh: Uber Eats上的两家独立餐厅，看起来是完全独立的企业，却以相同的价格销售带有相同描述的相同商品。

sentences.en: So I looked at another place that had a beer-battered cod for $16.95.
sentences.zh: 所以我又看了一家也有售价16.95美元的啤酒炸鳕鱼的地方。

sentences.en: Same description.
sentences.zh: 描述也是一样的。

sentences.en: And I looked at another place.
sentences.zh: 我又看了一家。

sentences.en: And he finds that, like, again and again.
sentences.zh: 他发现这种情况反复出现。

sentences.en: And so Eddie ends up ordering nine seemingly identical cod sandwiches from supposedly nine different restaurants, but they're all based at the same location.
sentences.zh: 于是埃迪最终从所谓的九家不同餐厅订购了九个看起来一模一样的鳕鱼三明治，但它们都位于同一个地址。

sentences.en: That is very weird.
sentences.zh: 这太奇怪了。

sentences.en: It's so weird.
sentences.zh: 太奇怪了。

sentences.en: And it makes you wonder why a single ghost kitchen would market the exact same sandwich but make it appear to come from all these different restaurants, right?
sentences.zh: 这让人不禁想问，为什么一个幽灵厨房要推销完全相同的三明治，却让它看起来像是来自所有这些不同的餐厅呢，对吧？

sentences.en: The way that it makes sense to me is that the way you use those apps, you sort of go into a restaurant and you explore it.
sentences.zh: 在我看来，这之所以说得通，是因为你使用这些应用程序的方式，你进入一家餐厅然后进行浏览。

sentences.en: It's not like you're necessarily looking for a cod sandwich and then you're comparing across restaurants.
sentences.zh: 并不是说你一定要找鳕鱼三明治，然后去比较各家餐厅。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: Almost like you're in a restaurant itself trying to decide.
sentences.zh: 就像你身处餐厅本身试图做决定一样。

sentences.en: And so if they want to sell that cod sandwich and they have lots of cod sandwiches available to be sold, it makes sense to put them in, you know,
sentences.zh: 所以如果他们想卖那个鳕鱼三明治，而且他们有很多鳕鱼三明治可以卖，那么把它放在，你知道，

sentences.en: as many restaurants as it seems appropriate.
sentences.zh: 尽可能多的餐厅里似乎是合理的。

sentences.en: Nine seems excessive.
sentences.zh: 九家似乎太多了。

sentences.en: Yeah, I think the whole thing has a kind of flood the zone feeling to me.
sentences.zh: 是的，我觉得整件事给我的感觉就像是“淹没区域”策略。

sentences.en: Yeah, totally.
sentences.zh: 是的，完全同意。

sentences.en: Like if someone's wanting a cod sandwich, the chance of them picking a cod sandwich from your kitchen goes up if you're offering the same sandwich but nine times.
sentences.zh: 就像如果有人想吃鳕鱼三明治，如果你提供了九次相同的选择，他们从你的厨房挑选鳕鱼三明治的机会就会增加。

sentences.en: And so, yeah, there's just a quality of these restaurants that feels like it has sort of tech optimization vibes.
sentences.zh: 所以，是的，这些餐厅有一种感觉，就像是某种技术优化。

sentences.en: It's like they're trying to SEO hack these delivery apps.
sentences.zh: 就像他们试图通过SEO（搜索引擎优化）来破解这些外卖应用程序一样。

sentences.en: And, you know, that's not surprising because many of these ghost kitchens are owned by tech startups.
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道，这并不奇怪，因为许多幽灵厨房都是由科技初创公司拥有的。

sentences.en: Oh, OK.
sentences.zh: 哦，好的。

sentences.en: They're not actually like some new form of restaurant.
sentences.zh: 它们实际上并不是什么新型餐厅。

sentences.en: They really are just another form of tech.
sentences.zh: 它们确实只是技术的另一种形式。

sentences.en: Yeah, and in a lot of ways, like I think you can find an individual owner of ghost kitchens, but there are big players involved with deep connections to the tech industry.
sentences.zh: 是的，在很多方面，我认为你可以找到幽灵厨房的个人所有者，但也有与科技行业有深厚联系的大玩家参与其中。

sentences.en: So Travis Kalanick, the former chief executive of Uber, has been working on cloud kitchens, which is a ghost kitchen startup.
sentences.zh: 比如优步（Uber）前首席执行官特拉维斯·卡兰尼克（Travis Kalanick）一直在研究云厨房（CloudKitchens），这是一家幽灵厨房初创公司。

sentences.en: Or there's also Reef Technology, a startup that includes multi-brand kitchens.
sentences.zh: 或者还有Reef Technology，一家包含多品牌厨房的初创公司。

sentences.en: This is very much a world where restaurants meet tech.
sentences.zh: 这确实是一个餐厅与科技相遇的世界。

sentences.en: And this trend is also intersecting with traditional brick and mortar restaurants in interesting ways.
sentences.zh: 而且这种趋势也正以有趣的方式与传统的实体餐厅交织在一起。

sentences.en: So there's another type of ghost kitchen I'll tell you about.
sentences.zh: 所以我还要告诉你另一种幽灵厨房。

sentences.en: And it actually runs out of existing restaurants.
sentences.zh: 它实际上是在现有餐厅内运营的。

sentences.en: OK, tell me more about those.
sentences.zh: 好的，再多告诉我一些关于那些厨房的事。

sentences.en: So what's happened is that some of the most popular chain restaurants out there, and these are places with actual restaurants you can eat in,
sentences.zh: 发生的情况是，一些最受欢迎的连锁餐厅，也就是那些你实际上可以进去用餐的餐厅，

sentences.en: they've decided to cash in on this trend.
sentences.zh: 它们决定利用这一趋势获利。

sentences.en: And what some of them have done is they've created new delivery-only restaurant brands that they are running out of their existing chain kitchens.
sentences.zh: 其中一些餐厅的做法是，它们创建了新的只做外卖的餐厅品牌，并在现有的连锁厨房中运营。

sentences.en: But it is not always clear to consumers that the delivery-only brand is affiliated with that chain.
sentences.zh: 但对于消费者来说，并不总是清楚这个只做外卖的品牌是否隶属于该连锁店。

sentences.en: So I thought to show you like how confusing this can be, that it might be fun to give you a little quiz.
